skill.name: aeon
skill.description: Guides time series machine learning with the aeon Python toolkit, including classification, regression, clustering, forecasting, anomaly detection, segmentation, and similarity search.
skill.summary: Use aeon methods for practical time series machine learning workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings were adjudicated as false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline code formatting, fixed aeon imports, and reference links. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration intent, or auto-executed command behavior was found in the cited files. The skill is documentation-oriented and should still be reviewed against the installed aeon version before use.

static_findings.snippet: Use grid search or random search:
1. **Fit on training data only**: Avoid data leakage
Categorize time series into predefined classes. See `references/classification.md` for complete algo
Predict continuous values from time series. See `references/regression.md` for algorithms.
Group similar time series without labels. See `references/clustering.md` for methods.
Predict future time series values. See `references/forecasting.md` for forecasters.
Identify unusual patterns or outliers. See `references/anomaly_detection.md` for detectors.
Partition time series into regions with change points. See `references/segmentation.md`.
Find similar patterns within or across time series. See `references/similarity_search.md`.
Transform time series for feature engineering. See `references/transformations.md`.
Specialized temporal distance measures. See `references/distances.md` for complete catalog.
Neural architectures for time series. See `references/networks.md`.
Load standard benchmarks and evaluate performance. See `references/datasets_benchmarking.md`.
3. **Check Data Format**: Aeon expects shape `(n_samples, n_channels, n_timepoints)`

content.value_statement: Time series work often needs algorithms beyond standard tabular machine learning. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through aeon methods for classification, forecasting, anomaly detection, segmentation, and related workflows.
actual_capabilities: Select aeon algorithms for classification, regression, clustering, forecasting, anomaly detection, segmentation, and similarity search.
Provide Python usage patterns for aeon estimators with scikit-learn compatible workflows.
Explain data preparation, normalization, imputation, and expected time series array shapes.
Compare distance metrics, transformations, benchmark datasets, and evaluation metrics for time series tasks.
Guide deep learning network choices and GPU setup for aeon models.
limitations: It does not include executable helper scripts or automated data processing.
Users must install aeon and compatible Python dependencies in their own environment.
Guidance may need verification against the installed aeon version and local data shapes.
It cannot guarantee model accuracy without validation and domain review.

use_cases.title: Create a Time Series Baseline
use_cases.description: Choose a first aeon model, prepare data, and define evaluation metrics for a labeled time series dataset.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Experiments
use_cases.description: Compare forecasting, anomaly detection, and segmentation options before implementing a repeatable experiment pipeline.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Aeon Algorithms
use_cases.description: Use documented datasets, resampling methods, and statistical tests to compare candidate algorithms.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Task
prompt_templates.prompt: I have temporal data with this goal: [describe goal]. Help me decide whether to use classification, regression, clustering, forecasting, anomaly detection, segmentation, or similarity search with aeon.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Aeon Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a simple aeon baseline for my dataset. The data shape is [shape], labels are [available or unavailable], and the success metric is [metric]. Include preprocessing and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Algorithms and Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare aeon algorithms for [task] under these constraints: [speed, accuracy, interpretability, data size]. Recommend metrics and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Benchmarking Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an aeon benchmarking plan for [problem]. Include dataset splits, resampling, baseline models, candidate models, statistical tests, and reporting criteria.

output_examples.input: I need to classify short sensor recordings into fault types.
output: Start with MiniRocketClassifier or RocketClassifier for a fast baseline.
Normalize each series, preserve train-test separation, and report accuracy plus confusion patterns.
Compare a distance-based nearest neighbor model if interpretability matters.

output_examples.input: I need to detect unusual subsequences in a single machine signal.
output: Use an anomaly detection workflow with a defined window size and held-out labeled events when possible.
Review score thresholds against domain costs before treating high scores as incidents.
Plot scores beside the original signal to check whether detections match meaningful changes.

output_examples.input: I want to compare forecasting approaches for monthly demand.
output: Begin with ARIMA or ETS as interpretable baselines.
Use rolling evaluation if the business process changes over time.
Track absolute error and percentage error, then inspect failure periods separately.

best_practices: Start with simple baselines before deep learning or large ensembles.
Normalize and impute using training data only to avoid leakage.
Choose metrics that match the task, data imbalance, and business cost.
anti_patterns: Do not use tabular models directly without checking temporal shape and alignment.
Do not tune on the test split or reuse transformed test data during training.
Do not choose deep learning models only because they are complex.

faq.question: What is aeon used for?
faq.answer: Aeon is a Python toolkit for machine learning on time series and other temporal data.

faq.question: Does this skill run models automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users can apply in their own Python environment.

faq.question: Can it help with unlabeled data?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers clustering, anomaly detection, segmentation, and similarity search for unlabeled or weakly labeled time series.

faq.question: Does it support forecasting?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains forecasting model choices and evaluation metrics for future value prediction.

faq.question: What data shape should I expect?
faq.answer: Many aeon workflows use samples, channels, and timepoints. The exact shape should match the selected estimator.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
